identity.name: AWS IAM & S3 Enumeration Sequence — Cloud Discovery Recon (SIM-CDR-021)
identity.summary: An AWS principal runs a cloud discovery sequence — an IAM enumeration burst then an S3 bucket enumeration sweep. The cloud_audit_emitter EAL plugin (aws) POSTs shape-true CloudTrail records to the operator collector so XSIAM raises the 'IAM Enumeration sequence' and 'AWS S3 Buckets enumeration activity' Analytics alerts, plus an ABIOC volume anomaly and a correlation on one caller ARN.
identity.description: Cloud attackers rarely act blind. Once a credential or role is obtained, the first move is enumeration: list the IAM users, roles, groups and attached policies to understand privilege and trust, then list the S3 buckets and their ACL/policy posture to find reachable data. Neither call is individually malicious — ListRoles and ListBuckets are made thousands of times a day by legitimate automation — so the signal is the SEQUENCE, VOLUME and BREADTH of discovery API calls from one principal in a short window, deviating from that principal's learned baseline. This card exercises the two XSIAM cloud-audit Analytics alerts named in the Cortex XSIAM Analytics Alert Reference for the AWS Audit Log (CloudTrail) data source — 'IAM Enumeration sequence' and 'AWS S3 Buckets enumeration activity' — mapped here to T1087.004 Account Discovery: Cloud Account (the IAM enumeration alert) and T1580 Cloud Infrastructure Discovery / T1619 Cloud Storage Object Discovery (the S3 enumeration alert), matching the driving cloud_audit_emitter's own technique mapping, plus a PANW-authored ABIOC that anchors the discovery-volume anomaly to the identity's learned CloudTrail baseline (behavioral-ML, causality chain), and a correlation rule that stitches the two enumeration alerts on the same caller ARN into one incident. The scenario DRIVES the cloud_audit_emitter analytics log-streamer to POST shape-true CloudTrail records into an operator-supplied collector so the detections fire without touching a real AWS tenant or reading any real account data. A validation XQL confirms the emitted records landed in cloud_audit_logs.

execution.framework_reference_id: SIM-CDR-021 — cloud_audit_emitter (provider=aws / CloudTrail) drives an IAM + S3 enumeration sequence into cloud_audit_logs.

prerequisites.description: An operator-supplied HTTP log collector (native XSIAM HTTP collector, Broker VM HTTP applet, or a Cribl/nginx forwarder) is wired into Cortex XSIAM as the AWS Audit Log (CloudTrail) source that normalises to the cloud_audit_logs dataset.
The cloud_audit_emitter EAL plugin is registered in the SimCore image.
prerequisites.check_command: python3 -m scripts.eal_simulator.cli describe cloud_audit_emitter | jq -e '.eal_targets | length > 0'

payload.code:
# Drive the cloud_audit_emitter analytics log-streamer to POST shape-true
# CloudTrail IAM + S3 enumeration records into the operator's collector.
set -euo pipefail
: "${COLLECTOR_URL:=https://collector.cortexsim-canary.invalid/logs/v1/event}"
: "${COLLECTOR_HOST:=collector.cortexsim-canary.invalid}"
cat > /tmp/cdr-021.yml <<YML
campaign_id: CMP-CDR-021
name: "CDR — AWS IAM & S3 enumeration sequence"
authorized_by: "domain-consultant@paloaltonetworks.com"
simulation_authorized: true
target_allowlist:
  - "${COLLECTOR_HOST}"
dry_run: false
steps:
  - step_id: iam-enum
    plugin: cloud_audit_emitter
    params:
      collector_url: "${COLLECTOR_URL}"
      provider: aws
      event_pattern: iam_enumeration
      iterations: 3
  - step_id: s3-enum
    plugin: cloud_audit_emitter
    params:
      collector_url: "${COLLECTOR_URL}"
      provider: aws
      event_pattern: s3_bucket_enumeration
      iterations: 3
YML
python3 -m scripts.eal_simulator.cli run /tmp/cdr-021.yml --live

abiocs.name: AWS Cloud-Discovery Volume Anomaly on a Learned Identity Baseline
abiocs.description: PANW-authored, auto-tuned behavioral-ML detection. Cortex learns each AWS principal's normal CloudTrail discovery-API profile (which enumeration calls it makes, how often, and how broad). This ABIOC fires when a principal's discovery-call volume and API breadth spike far above its learned baseline within a short window — the mass-enumeration deviation an attacker produces while mapping IAM trust and S3 exposure. No single ListRoles / ListBuckets call is a known-bad IOC; the catch is the deviation from the learned per-identity baseline, anchored to the identity's CloudTrail causality chain. The body below is the XQL-shaped proxy the ABIOC evaluates against the modeled baseline.
abiocs.logic:
dataset = cloud_audit_logs
| filter eventType = "AwsApiCall"
| filter eventName in ("ListUsers", "ListRoles", "ListPolicies", "GetAccountAuthorizationDetails", "ListAttachedRolePolicies", "ListBuckets", "GetBucketAcl", "GetBucketPolicy", "ListObjects")
| filter _time > to_timestamp(current_time() - 1800)
| comp count() as discovery_calls, count_distinct(eventName) as distinct_apis by userIdentity.arn, sourceIPAddress
| filter discovery_calls >= 8 and distinct_apis >= 5
| fields userIdentity.arn, sourceIPAddress, discovery_calls, distinct_apis
abiocs.causality_anchor: The principal's learned CloudTrail discovery-API baseline (the stable set of enumeration calls, their rate and breadth per caller ARN). The ABIOC anchors the volume/breadth deviation to that per-identity baseline and the caller-ARN causality chain, not to any single API call.

xql_queries.name: AWS IAM Enumeration Sequence
xql_queries.query:
dataset = cloud_audit_logs
| filter eventSource = "iam.amazonaws.com"
| filter eventName in ("ListUsers", "ListRoles", "ListPolicies", "ListGroups", "GetAccountAuthorizationDetails", "ListAttachedRolePolicies", "ListAttachedUserPolicies")
| filter _time > to_timestamp(current_time() - 900)
| comp count_distinct(eventName) as distinct_enum_calls, count() as iam_events by userIdentity.arn, sourceIPAddress
| filter distinct_enum_calls >= 4
| fields userIdentity.arn, sourceIPAddress, distinct_enum_calls, iam_events

xql_queries.name: AWS S3 Buckets Enumeration Activity
xql_queries.query:
dataset = cloud_audit_logs
| filter eventSource = "s3.amazonaws.com"
| filter eventName in ("ListBuckets", "ListObjects", "ListObjectsV2", "GetBucketAcl", "GetBucketPolicy", "GetBucketLocation")
| filter _time > to_timestamp(current_time() - 900)
| comp count_distinct(eventName) as distinct_s3_calls, count() as s3_events by userIdentity.arn, sourceIPAddress
| filter distinct_s3_calls >= 3
| fields userIdentity.arn, sourceIPAddress, distinct_s3_calls, s3_events

xql_queries.name: SIM-CDR-021 Emitted CloudTrail Landing Validation
xql_queries.query:
dataset = cloud_audit_logs
| filter _time > to_timestamp(current_time() - 900)
| filter cortexsim_run_id != null
| filter eventSource in ("iam.amazonaws.com", "s3.amazonaws.com")
| comp count() as emitted_records by eventSource, eventName
| sort desc emitted_records
| fields eventSource, eventName, emitted_records

correlation_rules.name: Cloud Reconnaissance Sequence — IAM Then S3 Enumeration by One Principal
correlation_rules.logic: XQL(AWS IAM Enumeration Sequence) AND XQL(AWS S3 Buckets Enumeration Activity) observed for the same userIdentity.arn within a 15-minute window, stitched into one cloud-reconnaissance-sequence incident anchored to the caller-ARN causality chain.

analytics_modules.note: The named XSIAM cloud-audit Analytics alert for the AWS Audit Log (CloudTrail) data source. Backed by the deployable XQL 'AWS IAM Enumeration Sequence' on this card (rule-based Analytics, cloud_audit_logs).

The named XSIAM cloud-audit Analytics alert for the AWS Audit Log (CloudTrail) data source. Backed by the deployable XQL 'AWS S3 Buckets Enumeration Activity' on this card (rule-based Analytics, cloud_audit_logs).

products.evidence_query: dataset = cloud_audit_logs | filter eventSource in ("iam.amazonaws.com", "s3.amazonaws.com") | filter eventName contains "List" or eventName contains "GetBucket" or eventName contains "GetAccountAuthorizationDetails" | comp count_distinct(eventName) as distinct_enum_calls by userIdentity.arn | filter distinct_enum_calls >= 4 | fields userIdentity.arn, distinct_enum_calls

threat_scenarios.name: Cloud reconnaissance — IAM & S3 enumeration sequence detection
threat_scenarios.description: Validate that Cortex XSIAM cloud-audit Analytics catches a discovery-stage enumeration sequence (IAM trust mapping followed by S3 exposure mapping) from a single AWS principal, and that the ABIOC + correlation fuse the two Analytics alerts into one cloud-reconnaissance incident.

threat_steps.objective: The IAM and S3 enumeration Analytics alerts fire and the correlation rule stitches them into one incident when the emitter drives a CloudTrail enumeration sequence.
preconditions: An operator-supplied HTTP collector is wired into XSIAM as the CloudTrail source (cloud_audit_logs).
The cloud_audit_emitter EAL plugin is registered in the SimCore image.
steps: Run the scenario so cloud_audit_emitter POSTs the IAM enumeration burst then the S3 enumeration sweep for one principal.
Confirm the 'IAM Enumeration sequence' and 'AWS S3 Buckets enumeration activity' Analytics alerts fire.
Confirm the ABIOC flags the discovery-volume anomaly and correlation CR-CDR-0021 raises one incident.
success_criteria: XQL 'AWS IAM Enumeration Sequence' returns at least one row for the emitting principal.
XQL 'AWS S3 Buckets Enumeration Activity' returns at least one row for the same principal.
Correlation `CR-CDR-0021` raises exactly one cloud-reconnaissance-sequence incident.

preventive_controls: Scope IAM roles and credentials to least privilege so a compromised principal cannot enumerate the full IAM inventory (deny iam:List*/iam:Get* and s3:ListAllMyBuckets outside the automation that needs it).
Enable S3 Block Public Access at the account level and manage bucket policies/ACLs centrally so enumeration yields no exploitable exposure.
Rotate and vault credentials; require MFA for the identities allowed to read account-wide IAM authorization details.
detection_engineering: Alert on a burst of distinct IAM discovery API calls (ListUsers/ListRoles/ListPolicies/GetAccountAuthorizationDetails/ListAttachedRolePolicies) from one caller ARN within a short window.
Alert on broad S3 enumeration (ListBuckets followed by GetBucketAcl/GetBucketPolicy/ListObjects across many buckets) from one caller ARN.

Baseline each principal's normal CloudTrail discovery profile and use the ABIOC to catch volume/breadth deviations rather than static thresholds; correlate the IAM and S3 enumeration alerts on the shared caller ARN to raise a single reconnaissance incident.
